q: Why did CAC increase yesterday? Check whether the change came from CPM, CTR, CPC, landing-page conversion, checkout conversion, product mix, or channel mix. Rank the drivers by likely contribution.
answer:
CAC rose a little yesterday: CAC was ₹2,154 on 2026-10-14 vs the weekday “usual” of ₹1,960 (+9.9%) and vs 2026-10-13 it was +2.5% (₹2,102 → ₹2,154). The change is small and within ordinary day-to-day variation; the diagnosis found no single supported cause in the data.

What’s behind it (ranked by likely contribution)
1. Channel / campaign mix (largest measured share): channel-level CAC moved up slightly and the mix shifted; this mechanically raised overall CAC by ~+2.5% versus the prior day. (Label from the diagnosis: moved but not a statistically supported single cause.)
2. Fewer new customers (volume drop): new customers fell (24 → 22, about −8.3%), which raised CAC by reducing the denominator. Diagnosis: contributed but within normal variation, not a supported cause.
3. Checkout conversion (small negative effect): checkout rate fell ~1.54% → 1.41% (−8.7%), which would raise CAC if sustained. Diagnosis: directionally consistent but inside the normal range (insufficient evidence to call it the cause).
4. CPM / CPC / CTR / landing-page cost (minor or offsetting): CPM and CPC were slightly lower (CPM −8.7%, CPC −8.4%), CTR almost unchanged; cost per landing-page-view ~flat. Diagnosis: these moved but their net effect was small and did not explain the increase.
5. Product mix / product net sales: ruled out — product-order net sales fell but stayed within its usual range and the diagnosis tests show it did not explain the CAC move.

Worth checking: channel- and campaign-level CAC and the handful of campaigns that shifted share yesterday (to confirm whether a small mix shift or one campaign caused the move).

Period: 2026-10-14 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-15
